review.rationale: Primary material independently challenged for relevance, support, actionable usefulness and limits. Changing documentation is due for re-observation after 90 days; this cadence is review policy, not a guarantee.

reasons.relevance: Recoverable observations directly address verbose agent context while keeping critical build and test facts available.
reasons.evidence: Pinned CCA 0.2 source supports normalization, redaction and recovery references; original stream bytes are not promised.
reasons.usefulness: Three saved log checks cover completion, failure and recovery, allowing a concrete bounded observation-retention trial.
reasons.clarity: Private storage, normalized recovery and unmeasured token or billing savings are stated without exaggerating the evidence.

need.query: How can I keep verbose build/test output out of agent context while preserving recoverable logs?

claims.text: The compressor stores a formatted observation before choosing compressed output; changed output carries a local raw_ref.

Formatting records command, exit code, stdout and stderr while stripping ANSI, applying redaction and trimming trailing whitespace. Recovery therefore concerns the normalized observation, not byte-exact original streams.
The README describes inspection/fallback passthrough and adapter failure returning the original tool result.

candidates.name: Keep recoverable normalized command observations
candidates.reason: Replay three saved nonsensitive logs containing repetition, a failure trace and dense structured output. Check diagnostic retention, omitted-text recovery, passthrough and fallback-read overhead. Keep estimates separate from provider billing.
limitations: No general token-saving or task-success benefit follows from the documentation. Preserve source logs separately when byte-exact streams matter; recovery files belong in private storage.
Documented capabilities acquired through primary-source research. Proposed trials have not been run; source support is separate from usefulness or comparative superiority.
